newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CAPELLO TO KEEP REAL AND MILAN ON HOLD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO TO KEEP REAL AND MILAN ON HOLD.

text.p: Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello, linked in Italy with his former club AC Milan next season, said in a newspaper interview on Friday he would not make a decision on his future until at least the middle of May.

"I am concentrating on my work, the present. I never look at the past or the future. On the latter, I will only speak once the league championship is over," Capello told the Italian daily Gazzetta dello Sport when asked about his future.
"I have said, and I repeat it, that it will not be before the middle of May."

Asked about reports that Real Madrid president Lorenzo Sanz had asked him to decide next Monday after Real's away match against Valencia, Capello said: "He must also have patience. Let's all stay calm, win the league as soon as possible and then I will decide. I also need to evaluate everything fully, for and against."
Milan president Silvio Berlusconi, for whom Capello won four Italian league titles and a European Cup, said recently he doubted Capello would leave Real if they won the Spanish title.
Real have a 10-point lead over rivals Barcelona at the top of the Spanish league. Milan are 12th in Italy and in danger of missing out on European club competition next season.
Asked about Berlusconi's comments, Capello merely replied: "Everyone is free to think and say what they want."
He added however that becoming the first coach to take Real to European Cup success since 1966 remained "one of my dreams".
Capello left Milan at the end of last season after taking them to their fourth league title in five years.
Uruguay's Oscar Washington Tabarez, his immediate replacement, resigned late last year and was in turn replaced by former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi.
